matt: Ran a quick cross-device microbenchmark this morning targeting small-batch tail latency across L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100. High-level summary: A100/H100 picks tiled-attn kernels at seqlen >= 192 and benefits from larger batching; L4/T4/A10 still prefer the fused-kernel path up to ~128, but we see KV-cache thrash on L4 when batch > 2 and seqlen > 64. Dump + notes below.

anya: Nice — can you paste the exact commands and a minimal perf snippet? :eyes: 

matt: Sure. Reproducer I used:
```
./tools/profiler --device L4 --model gpt-3-small --seqlen 80 --batch 3 --profile-mode latency --warmstart 0 --output /tmp/l4-run.log
./tools/profiler --device A100 --model gpt-3-small --seqlen 80 --batch 3 --profile-mode latency --warmstart 0 --output /tmp/a100-run.log
```
Key lines from L4 run:
```
P50: 14.2ms  P95: 82.1ms  median-kernel: fused-attn-v2  KV-cache-miss-rate: 0.18  swap-evictions: 23
```
A100 run:
```
P50: 9.6ms   P95: 45.8ms  median-kernel: tiled-attn-v3  KV-cache-miss-rate: 0.03  swap-evictions: 1
```

perf-bot: regression-detect: Comparing to baseline (commit abc123) — L4 P95 increased 18% for the 80/3 profile, alerting because this crosses our 10% perf-regression threshold. Link: https://perf.redwood/compare/2419802345

devon: I started a bisect. Early signal points to the autotune change landed in commit def456 — "heuristic-anneal: prefer_fused_on_small_devices=true". That heuristic bumps the fused-kernel score for L4/T4 in the 64-160 seqlen band which seems to force a path that increases KV churn.

rui: That matches what I observed in the memory traces — fused-attn buffers > tiled-attn by ~1.2GB on this model at seqlen 80, which pushes our allocator to evict prefix KV pages more often on 8GB-class cards. Evictions correlate with the P95 spikes.

anya: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) warm-start autotune: run 1-2 dummy inferences at deploy time to populate KV and prefer kernels that are KV-friendly for subsequent traffic; 2) add a memory-aware cap to the fused-kernel score so it won't be chosen when free_mem < threshold. Thoughts?

matt: I prototyped both. Quick notes: warmstart=2 reduced observed swap-evictions by ~60% on L4 and P95 improved ~9% vs the forced fused pick, but A100 lost some batching efficiency (P95 +2% overall) because warm-start prevented a large batch aggregation window.

devon: Can we make the autotuner device-aware and cost-sensitive simultaneously? Proposed rule: if device_family in [L4,T4,A10] and free_mem < 6GB and seqlen > 64 -> prefer kv-friendly kernel unless latency delta <= 5%. Implement as a lightweight scoring penalty rather than a hard override.

rui: I can sketch the heuristic: penalty = max(0, (6GB - free_mem)/6GB) * baseline_score_multiplier; clamp penalty to 0.3. Also add a warmstart_boost for kernels that avoid extra allocations.

anya: That sounds good. Also we should add a metric to detect KV thrash: "kv_evictions_per_minute" and an alert when it climbs over baseline+5. That will help catch regressions early.

devon: I'll open a PR to add device_priors, warmstart param, and the KV thrash metric. Drafting branch: feat/autotune-device-priors. I'll include a toggle so we can flip it in canary.

perf-bot: perf-job: ran canary comparison after applying warmstart=2 + device_priors on staging L4 pool: P95 improvement 11% vs pre-change, cost delta +1.8% on A100 staging pool. Full report: https://perf.redwood/report/2419802345/canary

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: cluster=staging-inference, nodes=20, config=autotune-device-priors, rollout=gradual :rocket:

matt: After canary finished, results look positive. Let's land the PR behind a runtime flag and enable for L4/T4/A10 pools only. We'll monitor kv_evictions_per_minute and tail-latency for 24h before flipping for A100.

anya: Agreed. Two follow-ups: 1) add a small e2e reproducer to infra that runs the profiler nightly on each device family (seqlen {32,80,256}, batch {1,2,4}) so we can see drift; 2) add a short doc blurb in eng-runtime/README about "autotune warmstart" and the rationale.

devon: PR opened: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/5423 — includes tests + opt-in flag + canary config.

rui: I'll wire the kv_evictions metric to the perf dashboard and create an alert policy with a 15m window.

matt: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll keep the raw traces in /artifacts/perf/2419802345 for 7 days if you need deeper dumps. :thumbsup:

anya: Thanks — looks like a nice win for small-GPU customers. Keep an eye on cost vs latency tradeoff though.

devon: Will follow up with a short postmortem if anything regresses during the 24h canary.

perf-bot: note: baseline hashes referenced: abc123 (stable), def456 (heuristic-anneal change).

matt: Closing for now — will reopen if alerts fire.
